q: 1. The paper size of A4 is
explain: As per ISO 216 A-series standard, A4 measures 210 mm × 297 mm.

q: 2. The width of the standard A-series drawing paper such as A4, A3, A2 … is
options: 1/√2 times the length of the paper
1/√3 times the length of the paper
1/√4 times the length of the paper
1/√5 times the length of the paper
explain: The A-series is designed so length:width = √2:1, i.e. the width is 1/√2 times the length, preserving the aspect ratio when the sheet is halved.

q: 3. Working/ drawing space on the paper is determined by
explain: Border lines are drawn on the sheet to define the actual area available for the technical drawing and to provide a frame for the work.

q: 4. In the engineering system of paper sizes, which of the following is "A2" size?
5. A typical layout of drawing sheet do not contain .............
explain: Standard drawing sheet layouts include centering marks, orientation marks, and identification/title marks, but 'trimming marks' are not part of the standard sheet layout elements defined by drawing standards.

q: 6. The paper size of A3 is
explain: Standard ISO paper sizes: A3 is 297mm x 420mm (double the size of A4).

q: 7. Which of the following is preferred containing the statement "All dimensions are in millimeters unless otherwise specified" .............
explain: General notes such as the units statement are conventionally placed within the title block of the drawing sheet.

q: 8. Size of A4 size paper is
explain: A4 is the most common paper size, measuring exactly 210mm by 297mm.

q: 9. "A" series of paper has length of width ratio of approximately .............
explain: ISO A-series paper sizes maintain a constant aspect ratio of √2:1, which allows each size to be halved into the next smaller size while preserving the same proportions.

q: 10. Number of equal pieces of A4 size paper from A0 is equal to
explain: Each step in the A-series halves the area. $A0 \rightarrow A1 \rightarrow A2 \rightarrow A3 \rightarrow A4$. That is $2^4 = 16$ sheets.

q: 11. Number of orientation mark generally contained by a drawing sheet is .............
explain: A standard drawing sheet layout generally includes two orientation marks to indicate the correct viewing direction of the sheet.

q: 12. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A1 (drawing sheet).
explain: One A0 sheet is equivalent to two A1 sheets placed side-by-side.

q: 13. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A2 (drawing sheet).
explain: Following the division rule ($2^2$), A0 is four times the size of A2.

q: 14. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A3 (drawing sheet).
explain: Following the division rule ($2^3$), A0 is eight times the size of A3.

q: 15. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A4 (drawing sheet).
explain: Following the division rule ($2^4$), A0 is sixteen times the size of A4.

q: 16. During draw a drawing we start from
options: top to bottom of drawing paper
bottom to top of drawing paper
right to left of drawing paper
left to right of drawing paper
explain: Drawing from top-to-bottom and left-to-right (for right-handed users) prevents the hand or tools from smudging lines that were already drawn.

q: 17. To facilitate extension, entries in the table should begain from
explain: Filling tables from bottom upward leaves room at the top for later entries, allowing the table to be extended easily.

q: 18. The size of title block of all size drawing sheet is
explain: As per standard drafting practice, the title block occupies a fixed area of 185 mm × 65 mm regardless of sheet size.

q: 19. The ratio of distance on the drawing sheet and corresponding actual distance of the object is known as
explain: This ratio, drawing distance to actual distance, is by definition called the Representative Factor (RF).

q: 20. When only one drawing is to be made then its position should be .............
explain: A single drawing on a sheet is conventionally positioned at the centre of the paper for balanced composition and to leave adequate margins on all sides.

q: 21. The size of title block of all size drawing sheet is .............
explain: As per drawing standards, the standard title block size used uniformly across all drawing sheet sizes is 185 mm × 65 mm.

q: 22. Which of the following is the largest size of a engineering drawing sheet?
explain: In the ISO A-series, the sheet number decreases as size increases; A0 (841×1189 mm) is the largest of the options listed.

q: 23. Tracing paper is also named as .............
explain: Tracing paper used in drafting is also generically referred to as drafting media, a term covering various transparent/translucent sheet materials used for tracing drawings.

q: 24. Title block gives the information about:
explain: The title block consolidates all key drawing information: title, scale, serial/sheet number, and more.

q: 25. In standard A series drawing sheet, the ratio of length of shorter side to longer side is equal to:
explain: The A-series sheets maintain a constant aspect ratio of shorter side to longer side equal to 1:√2.

q: 26. The width of the standard A-series drawing paper such A4, A3, A2 ..... is .............
options: 1/√2 times the length of the paper
1/√3 times the length of the paper
1/√4 times the length of the paper
1/√5 times the length of the paper
explain: Since the A-series maintains a length:width ratio of √2:1, the width equals the length divided by √2, i.e., 1/√2 times the length.

q: 27. What is the standard size (in mm) of A3 size drawing sheet?
explain: As per ISO A-series, A3 measures 297 mm × 420 mm.

q: 28. The 'title block' is provided in a drawing sheet at:
explain: By drafting convention the title block is placed in the bottom-right hand corner of the sheet for easy reference when folded.

q: 29. The measurement of standard A2 size drawing sheet in mm is .............
explain: Standard ISO A2 sheet size is 420 mm × 594 mm, consistent with the halving pattern of the A-series from A0 downward.

q: 30. The preparation of a successful drawing depends on the ............. of drawing sheet.
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'letters' is marked correct — implying that clear, standardized lettering/notation is emphasized as central to a successful, communicative drawing.

q: 31. The most important material for drawing is .............
explain: The two most basic and essential materials for any drawing work are paper (the drawing surface) and pencil (the drawing instrument).

q: 32. Drawing is the ............. of Engineers.
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'Machine' is marked correct for this item; conventionally, engineering drawing is described as the 'universal language of engineers,' but the given key selects option (c).

q: 33. "Title Block" is placed at bottom right hand corner of the drawing which gives information about
explain: The title block is the metadata center of a drawing, containing names, dates, scales, and identification numbers.

q: 34. Title block in drawing sheets gives the information about
explain: The title block consolidates the drawing title, scale and serial/sheet number along with other reference details.

q: 35. The size of drawing board required for A0 sheet size (in mm) is
explain: A board of about 1500 × 1000 × 25 mm is large enough to accommodate an A0 sheet (841 × 1189 mm) with margins.

q: 36. Title book of drawing sheet contains
explain: The title block contains all key reference details: drawing title, drawing number and scale, among others.

q: 37. *In standard A series drawing sheet, the ratio of length of shorter side to longer side
explain: ISO 216 standard (A series) uses a constant aspect ratio of 1 to the square root of 2 ($1:\sqrt{2}$) so that the proportions remain the same when the sheet is folded in half.

q: 38. The best drawing paper used for water colour is :
explain: Though handmade paper is traditionally used, the answer key specifies tracing/technical sheets in this specific engineering context.

q: 39. The selection of suitable scale and allotment of proper space for margin, title block, revision panel, folding marks, etc. on the drawing sheet is known as :
explain: Layout refers to the organized arrangement of all required elements on a drawing sheet.

q: 40. The size of the title block of all sizes of drawing sheet is :
explain: According to Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the standard size for a title block is 185 mm x 65 mm.

q: 41. The normal size of drawing sheet referred as 'A1' is:
explain: As per ISO A-series, A1 measures 594 mm × 841 mm.

q: 42. Building working drawing are generally prepared in drawing paper of:
explain: Building working drawings, which need to show adequate detail for large structures, are generally prepared on A1 size sheets.

q: 43. *Working drawings:
options: must provide complete information to produce the object
should be supplemented by further details
explain: A working drawing must contain all necessary dimensions, notes, and views for a manufacturer to build the part without further questions.

q: 44. The paper size is
explain: 297 × 420 mm corresponds to the standard A3 sheet size, matching the correct option given.

q: 45. Church in a drawing sheet is symbolized as:
explain: On maps/plans, a church is conventionally shown as a small figure/symbol (often a cross-topped icon) rather than a plain point.

q: 46. The size of A2 size paper is:
explain: As per ISO A-series, A2 measures 420 mm × 594 mm.

q: 47. The paper size of A4 is (in mm)
explain: As per ISO A-series, A4 measures 210 mm × 297 mm.

q: 48. Most prevailing size of drawing sheets used in preparation of municipal drawing for building permit is .............
explain: Municipal building permit drawings are commonly prepared and submitted on A1 size sheets, balancing detail and manageable size for official records.

q: 49. The following is not included in title block of drawing sheet
explain: The title block typically records sheet number, scale, and sheet size, but the method of projection is shown separately (often via a projection symbol), not as a standard title block entry.

q: 50. The ISO A0 size of drawing is defined as having an area of .............
explain: The ISO A0 sheet size is defined such that its area equals exactly 1 square meter, from which all other A-series sizes are derived by successive halving.
